newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes weaker on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes weaker on arbitrage play.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed sharply weaker at 26.278 to the dollar from Wednesday's 26.246 on arbitrage play, traders said.

Banks bought dollars in the hope of selling it back on Tuesday while still holding on to their pesos for four days and earn on the domestic interest rates. Trades done on Thursday will be settled on Tuesday because of the long weekend.
The foreign exchange market will be closed on Friday and Monday in view of the APEC meetings. It will reopen on Tuesday.
"Banks are playing on the swap points," one trader said.
The peso depreciation was further aided by Central Bank which started buying dollars at 26.244 in large volume.
Banks caught on the buying spree and lowered the rate further to its intra-day low of 26.278, another trader said.
He said the Central Bank was replenishing its forex reserves after selling large volume in the past days to dampen the peso's fall.
